title: PIFS-Rec: Process-In-Fabric-Switch for Large-Scale Recommendation System Inferences
problem: DLRMs suffer from severe bandwidth bottlenecks due to large embedding table vector sizes and concurrent accesses. Existing CXL-based systems have unresolved performance bottlenecks that prevent effective DLRM acceleration.
motivation: DLRMs consume the majority of AI inference cycles in modern datacenters, making their optimization critical for system efficiency and cost.
method: PIFS-Rec solves a critical bottleneck in recommendation systems: embedding tables (large lookup tables that map items to their numerical representations) are enormous, and shipping all that data through the network to a CPU or GPU uses massive amounts of bandwidth and slows everything down. Instead, the system performs embedding lookups directly on the CXL fabric switch's downstream ports—the connections in the hardware fabric that links different system components. By doing this computation right where the data lives, much less data has to travel through the network, which reduces latency and frees up bandwidth.
key_novelty: Executing embedding lookups on the CXL fabric switch's downstream ports instead of moving the data to separate processors.
contributions: In-depth characterization of industry-scale DLRM workloads on CXL-ready systems identifying memory and bandwidth bottlenecks
PIFS-Rec scheme implementing near-data processing through fabric switch downstream ports
Achieves 3.89x latency reduction versus Pond (industry-standard CXL system) and 2.03x versus BEACON
Optimizes memory and bandwidth scalability for large-scale recommendation inference
limitations: Scalability to multiple fabric switches and applicability beyond recommendation systems not discussed.
primary_theme: Fabric switch acceleration for DLRM inference
